_readme: Copy to ~/.config/memory-arbiter/config.json and edit local paths.

Since 0.15.0 configuration is file-only and this is the complete 18-key user surface. Engine params, timeouts, thresholds, and caps are frozen constants (memory_arbiter/constants.py); 0.14.x keys that no longer exist are ignored with a 'no longer configurable' warning. Only six launch-context env vars remain (MEMORY_ARBITER_CONFIG/DB_PATH/BACKUP_JSONL/MCP_TRANSPORT/CLIENT/AGENT_ID); every other MEMORY_ARBITER_* variable is no longer read.

client and agent_id are REQUIRED with no built-in defaults: the MCP server refuses to start when either is missing or blank. Under stdio this configured identity is the process-level caller identity used for attribution and policy decisions; streamable-http takes caller identity from the per-request X-Mema-Client / X-Mema-Agent-Id headers instead.

embedding.model_path IS the intent to enable sqlite-vec evidence recall — there is no vec.enabled/provider/dim knob any more. The vector dimension comes from the model itself; switching to a model with a different dimension drops and rebuilds the vector tables at the new dimension at startup.
semantic_conflict.model_path enables the local Qwen2.5-0.5B runtime: it loads at startup and stays resident (preload/resident are frozen true); scan is broad and write-time notice is strict.
This example explicitly keeps semantic_conflict.enabled=false: editing model_path alone will not enable it; set enabled=true or remove enabled to use model-path auto-enable.
The HTTP endpoint path is fixed /mcp and request bodies are capped at 4 MB; ranking is fixed hybrid.
All isolation modes normalize workspace_canonical; none disables ACL only.
mema setup writes a smaller embedding-only template; it intentionally does not mirror every optional key in this reference example.
